high_court_outcome.value: Partly allowed appeals, converted death sentences to life imprisonment

quotes.text: The Division Bench of the High Court partly allowed the appeals preferred by Mohan Lal and others, who were convicted under Sections 302 and 460 IPC and sentenced to death, acquitting Mohan Lal of the charges framed against him under Sections 302 and 460 IPC and as far as the other accused persons of the same category were concerned, the sentence of death was converted to life sentence and, resultantly, the death reference was declined.
Dismissing all the appeals, the Court HELD: 1.1. It is settled in law that mere delay in lodging the First Information Report cannot be regarded by itself as fatal to the case of the prosecution.

neutral_facts.value: The incident involved five persons being killed by blows with swords, gandasis, and sticks. The crime was allegedly motivated by a prior incident where the son of a village Sarpanch was murdered, and the Sarpanch suspected the deceased were involved. The accused formed an unlawful assembly with a common object to kill the deceased. The FIR was delayed, but the explanation for the delay was not implausible. Witnesses, who had lost family members, testified about the weapons used, the assault, and injuries inflicted. The trial court convicted 17 accused, including six with death sentences and 11 with life imprisonment, while acquitting the rest. The High Court partially allowed appeals, converting death sentences to life imprisonment and acquitting some accused.
